observed_symptoms: [Sin respuesta sintetizada] when all LLM models fail

1_intent_detection.mechanism: AGENT_KEYWORDS list -> _AGENT_PATTERNS compiled regex, used in _should_use_agent()
1_intent_detection.before_any_regression: Same logic present since at least db21ae89
1_intent_detection.current_HEAD: Same logic, unchanged in all commits inspected
1_intent_detection.finding: Intent detection is NOT regressed. AGENT_KEYWORDS includes \bdiagnostica\b, \bmuestra\b, \bcambios\b, \bultimos\b, \bui\b, \bherramienta\b — all present in the observed prompts. This means _should_use_agent() correctly returns True for both prompts via _AGENT_PATTERNS keyword match.

2_routing.before_regression: _route_to_agent() tried tool01_router first (deterministic), then many fastpaths (estado del sistema, trading, dashboard, etc.), then AgentLoop
2_routing.current_HEAD: Same structure. tool01_router tries 5 tools (health_check, git_status, list_directory, read_file, write_file). Neither 'diagnostica con herramientas' nor 'muestra cuales fueron los ultimos cambios' match any of the 5 tool patterns.
2_routing.finding: Both observed prompts fall THROUGH tool01_router (no match) AND fall through all named fastpaths (no match for these exact strings). They then fall into AgentLoop. This was always the case — _TOOL01_ROUTER_PATTERNS never included a 'diagnostic_general' or 'cambios_ui' tool.
2_routing.root_cause_here: PARTIAL — _TOOL01_ROUTER_PATTERNS is too narrow for diagnostic requests
2_routing.note: TOOL01 only covers: health_check, git_status, list_directory, read_file, write_file. There is no 'diagnostic' tool in TOOL01.

3_tool_selection.mechanism: AgentLoop uses LLM (kimi_cloud->codex->deepseek14b->llama8b) to decide which tool to call each step
3_tool_selection.before_regression: Same — AgentLoop has always been LLM-driven for tool selection
3_tool_selection.current_HEAD: Same — if LLM is unavailable, each step fails to produce an action -> result stays None -> loop exhausts steps
3_tool_selection.finding: When Ollama is down AND external APIs (codex/gpt4/claude) are not configured, every LLM step fails. The loop runs 12 steps each timing out. This was always a latent risk but only surfaces when the full LLM pool is unavailable.
3_tool_selection.root_cause_here: YES — No LLM preflight before entering the loop

4_agent_loop.before_regression: Same _COMPLEX_SIGNALS regex exists in all commits including db21ae89
4_agent_loop.finding: 'diagnostica' triggers complexity=complex in ALL commits since at least db21ae89 (the first commit that added MetaPlanner). This is not a regression — it was always 12 steps for diagnostic requests. But since those 12 steps each depended on LLM, when LLM is down it always consumed all 12 steps.
4_agent_loop.root_cause_here: CONTRIBUTING — complexity=complex is appropriate for the task but no LLM preflight means 12 timeouts occur

5_llm_fallback.before_regression: Message: '*[Sin respuesta sintetizada — todos los modelos LLM fallaron]*'
5_llm_fallback.current_HEAD_with_E2_patch: Message: 'LLM pool no disponible. Ollama: posiblemente caido.'
5_llm_fallback.finding: The original fallback message was cryptic but technically correct. The E2 patch improved the message text only — this part of the E2 patch is acceptable cosmetic improvement.

6_governance.before_regression: _TOOL01_ROUTER_PATTERNS had 4 tools (no write_file). HEAD added write_file.
6_governance.e2_patch_problem: Added subprocess.create_subprocess_shell() call directly in session.py — bypasses tool governance, audit trail, and permission gate. Also adds 17-keyword list hardcoded in business logic.
6_governance.finding: The fastpath added by E2 violates the existing tool governance model. git diff --stat should be executed via the existing run_command tool registered in the executor, not via raw subprocess in session.py.

7_ui_compatibility.chat_d_impact: CHAT-D modified only index.html (frontend). No backend routing changed.
7_ui_compatibility.finding: CHAT-D did NOT cause or contribute to the max_steps_reached regression. The backend routing was identical before and after CHAT-D.

summary.true_root_cause: Two compounding issues: (A) _TOOL01_ROUTER_PATTERNS does not include a 'diagnostic' entry for general diagnostic requests — they fall through to AgentLoop. (B) AgentLoop has no LLM pool preflight check — when all models in the chain fail, the loop wastes all 12 steps timing out instead of exiting early.
summary.not_regressed_vs_previous_commits: The logic in _should_use_agent, _classify_complexity, _TOOL01_ROUTER_PATTERNS, and _route_to_agent is functionally identical across all inspected commits (810a052d, 0a00f565, db21ae89, 6ee95ff2). This is a latent design gap exposed only when the full LLM pool is down.
e2_fastpath_problems: Hardcoded 17-keyword list in business logic instead of formal tool registration
subprocess.create_subprocess_shell() bypasses tool governance, audit trail, permission gate
glob() and os.path in session.py instead of using registered list_directory/read_file tools
route='agent_tool_fastpath' is not a recognized route type in the system
Masks the real gap rather than fixing it
